The "death" of the ego is "kind" of a way to put it. I can see why people might be confused. But, it's more Stoic in nature. You aren't killing the ego, because it is an indivisible part of human nature. So, to completely kill the ego would be in effect killing the person. That is destructive.

The Ego is basically "Who we are". It's purpose is to balance out the impulsive nature of the Id and the oppressive nature of the Super-Ego. So, the Ego is not a bad thing. But, it does need to be properly trained to function as a useful tool. Otherwise, if the Id and the Super-Ego is left without checks in place, one will out compete the other and a person will fall to destructive habits.

So, if the Ego is "Who a person is", a Buddhist is a person who tries to create a healthy balance between the Id and the Super Ego. This isn't killing the Ego, it is using the Ego to define himself as a healthy and rationally balanced person.

If you must think of it in terms of "Killing the Ego". Think of it as "Killing the old / bad Ego you once were", and replacing it with "A new better model which will make you a better person". In effect, you are killing the old "Wife Beater" / "Alcoholic" / "<insert the 'bad' aspects of who you were>" / etc. and replacing it with an entirely new you (Ego) who is trying to become the Übermench (Buddha).

And notice that in no point in explaining any of this have I even touched on the concept of Nirvana. I don't place the concept of Nirvana in any high regard as a goal. But, Nirvana is basically in-line with Atheist thought in that when you die, you are basically "obliterated". This is why, as an Atheist, I don't put any weight in it.

Nirvana is more of a thought experiment to prepare religious people who are attached to existence to the point that they need to believe in an afterlife. An Atheist has an "lower barrier to entry" into Buddhism, because he has no such attachments and thus can move on to the purpose of "non-attachment" which is focusing on this life. The person who does believe in an afterlife must move past that attachment in order to focus on this life.
